summary: The 2D screening label is illustrative_2d_only, but the gate did not pass (input_gate_pass false, scientific_gate_pass false, simulation_allowed false), so Studio did not run: simulation status is skipped because a custom experiment needs 1–128 blocks and a power_w object. The experiment was a custom 2D steady case with empty floorplan and power_w, so no Studio result and no transient trace exist. The paper scenario is the Ascend 910 System row of Table I (RLPlanner reward -7.4063, wirelength 18130 as labelled mm, runtime 7773 s), with a reported maximum temperature of 77.12 C from the fast thermal model. comparison_valid is false, so there is no numerical comparison with 77.12 C and no claim of replication or agreement. The 2-page paper gives no chiplet names, geometry, per-block or total power, or power-splitting rule, so no floorplan could be built. Package, material and cooling boundary conditions, the workload, and the steady/transient regime are also unstated. The 77.12 C value is a single maximum with an unstated spatial location, produced by a fast LTI thermal-resistance model approximating HotSpot (MAE 0.25 K) rather than a full-field solver. The RL optimizer and reward cannot be reproduced by a Studio run, which could at most evaluate a given floorplan. The ServeTheHome reference is not a pinned asset and the GitHub URL is missing. Several evidence items lack valid page or asset locators and the adversarial and independent reviews are unresolved. The only defensible conclusion is that this paper is not currently usable for a quantitative Studio comparison; at best it supports a qualitative remark that floorplan placement affects maximum temperature.
limitations: Studio did not run, so there is no simulated temperature, field or trace to compare.
The custom 2D steady experiment has no blocks and no power_w, so it fails input validation.
No numerical comparison with 77.12 C is valid: location, aggregation, regime and boundary assumptions are unmatched or unknown.
The Ascend 910 floorplan geometry and per-block power are not reported in the paper, and no power-splitting rule is published.
Interposer, package and material stack, heat sink, convection and ambient conditions are unspecified.
The paper does not state whether 77.12 C is steady-state, and it reports no transient behavior; a custom steady run would have no transient trace.
The published value comes from a fast LTI thermal-resistance model approximating HotSpot, not from a solver comparable to Studio.
The PPO+RND optimizer, reward weights, and temperature limit T0 are not reproduced or given, so the published floorplan cannot be regenerated.
The wirelength column is labelled mm but has values in the thousands, so its unit is uncertain.
Linked assets (ServeTheHome page, GitHub repository) are unpinned or have no URL, and several evidence items lack valid locators.
Adversarial and independent review checks are unresolved, and the result is not independently verified.
This is not a replication, and 3D stacking and thermomechanical or reliability effects are outside scope.
